limitations: Used only the serialized input; source excerpts and curator fact transcriptions were not independently verified. No tools, external knowledge, or remembered target results were used.
The 2026-05-15 cutoff is the information-availability boundary. All supplied historical releases and admitted evidence precede it; no target-quarter outcomes are supplied or inferred.

This is an illustrative FY2026 Q4 scenario reconstruction, not an official budget. Frozen control assumptions remain analyst judgments, and market evidence supplies no calibrated company elasticities.
Historical income-statement inputs are treated as reported GAAP figures; organic growth is a distinct adjusted measure. Core earnings reconciliations are absent.
Cash, debt maturities, refinancing exposure, procurement timing, geographic currency exposure, working capital, operational unit counts, and headcount detail are absent.
Quarterly cash conversion and capital spending are seasonal. Historical ratios are reference points, not annualized forecasts.
Diluted shares inferred from attributable net income divided by rounded EPS are approximate denominators, not reported share counts.

issues: FY2026 Q3 arithmetic discrepancies: gross profit 10,513 minus SG&A 5,936 equals 4,577, versus reported operating income 4,576; operating income plus component nonoperating income 414 equals 4,990, versus pretax 4,989; pretax 4,989 minus taxes 1,039 equals 3,950, versus NI 3,951. Preserve supplied values and flag USD 1 million residuals; their cause is unverified.

FY2025 Q3 also has USD 1 million residuals: sales less product costs equals 10,082 versus gross profit 10,081; gross profit less SG&A equals 4,557 versus operating income 4,558; operating income plus signed income components equals 4,662 versus pretax 4,661. FY2026 Q1 component pretax bridge gives 6,035 versus reported 6,034. These do not justify silent corrections.

Other income is labeled 'operating' in several excerpts but 'non-operating' in FY2025 Q4. Contract treatment places it below operating income; classification cannot be independently resolved from the supplied packet.

The frozen control is supplied and should remain unchanged: base sales growth 0.04, gross margin 0.49, SG&A ratio 0.282, net nonoperating income 150, tax rate 0.205, noncontrolling income 18, diluted shares 2,405, cash conversion 1.3, capex ratio 0.05. These are assumptions, not reported observations.

PG06 and PG08 support combined cost downside, not additive full shocks. The supplied -20 to -80 bp margin range is analyst judgment. Latest Q3 historical compression belongs to the history refresh; any market adjustment must be incremental to that refreshed control.

PG06's annual tariff headwind 400 and FX tailwind 200 are after tax and unchanged from PG01. Do not assign them wholly to Q4, divide mechanically by four, treat FX earnings guidance as sales translation, or duplicate them through macro sensitivities.

PG02/PG04 and PG07/PG09 overlap through household demand. CPI, nominal PCE, real PCE, and personal-care inflation do not establish P&G pricing or volume elasticities. Use a joint scenario sensitivity rather than mechanical pass-through or summed demand shocks.
PG10 peer growth does not establish P&G market-share losses or gains. Any competitive selling-cost or volume sensitivity is illustrative; unrelated base drivers should remain unchanged.
PG05 reports a policy rate, not P&G borrowing costs. Floating-rate balances and refinancing timing are absent; no immediate earnings charge or numeric debt sensitivity is supported.
PG05's overlap note mentions an annual interest/tax headwind in PG01, but PG01's supplied factual extracts contain no such amount. That additional claim is unsupported here.

Organic annual guidance of 0–4% is not a hard constraint on quarterly reported sales growth. Reported growth includes FX and other adjustments, while historical percentage contributions are approximate.

No evidence-based numeric updates are supplied for taxes, noncontrolling interests, share repurchases, cash conversion, or capex. Contract bounds are guardrails, not estimates; adverse scenarios can increase expense ratios, taxes, shares, and capex while reducing profitability.
